extracted.intended_audience: pharmaceutical companies, regulatory affairs professionals, healthcare stakeholders, EMA observers and the general public interested in CHMP procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) roles, assessment standards, publication and meeting procedures, governance documents and composition relevant to EMA human medicines regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralised procedure responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: In the centralised procedure, CHMP is responsible for: conducting the initial assessment of EU-wide marketing authorisation applications; assessing modifications or extensions ('variations') to an existing marketing authorisation; considering the recommendations of the Agency's Pharmacovigilance Risk Assessment Committee on the safety of medicines on the market and when necessary, recommending to the European Commission changes to a medicine's marketing authorisation, or its suspension or withdrawal from the market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the core functions of CHMP for the centralised authorisation route; applicants and stakeholders should expect CHMP to perform initial scientific assessments, handle variations, and act on PRAC safety recommendations including recommending regulatory actions to the European Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral procedures / harmonised position
rubrics_metrics.description: CHMP also evaluates medicines authorised at national level referred to EMA for a harmonised position across the EU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When Member States refer nationally authorised medicines to EMA, CHMP provides an EU-wide assessment to reach a harmonised regulatory position; see 'Referral procedures' for details on when and how referrals occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to medicine development and regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: CHMP and its working parties contribute to the development of medicines and medicine regulation by: providing scientific advice to companies researching and developing new medicines; preparing scientific guidelines and regulatory guidance to help pharmaceutical companies prepare marketing authorisation applications for human medicines; cooperate with international partners on the harmonisation of regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CHMP issues proactive scientific advice and guidance documents intended to improve development programs and align regulatory expectations; companies should consult CHMP guidance when preparing applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific assessment standards (quality, safety, efficacy, risk–benefit)
rubrics_metrics.description: CHMP's assessments are based on a comprehensive scientific evaluation of data. They determine whether the medicine meets the necessary quality, safety and efficacy requirements and that it has a positive risk-benefit balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations focus on the totality of evidence addressing quality, safety and efficacy and conclude on the medicine's favourable risk–benefit for the intended use; applicants should ensure dossiers address these dimensions comprehensively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal peer-review safeguard
rubrics_metrics.description: An internal peer-review system safeguards the accuracy and validity of the opinions of the committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CHMP uses internal peer review to validate scientific opinions and ensure robustness of assessments prior to publication or recommendation; this is an explicit quality control mechanism for opinions and outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency: publication of agendas, minutes and highlights
rubrics_metrics.description: EMA publishes the agendas, minutes and highlights of the CHMP plenary meetings. The Committee has been publishing meeting reports summarising the main outcomes of its meetings since it was established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders can access agendas, minutes and highlights to follow CHMP deliberations and decisions; publication of meeting reports supports transparency of outcomes and decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing rules for CHMP outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Agendas: Before start of Committee plenary. Minutes: After Committee plenary where minutes are adopted. Meeting highlights: Friday after Committee plenary. PROM agendas: Week before Committee plenary (note: as of June 2023, CHMP no longer publishes the PROM meeting agendas). PROM minutes: After current month's Committee plenary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These timing rules indicate when stakeholders can expect to see CHMP materials published; note the policy change on PROM agendas (no longer published since June 2023) and where PROM agenda information can instead be found (in PROM minutes).

rubrics_metrics.name: IRIS publication of regulatory-procedure data (Excel)
rubrics_metrics.description: As of March 2025, EMA publishes information - in Excel format - on the start of the procedures for extension applications and for type II variations that propose an extension of the authorised indication handled in IRIS. Starting with January 2025, EMA is publishing in Excel format the CHMP agenda annex with the regulatory procedures handled in IRIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change follows the transition of post-authorisation regulatory procedures to IRIS and EMA's digitalisation efforts; publishing machine-readable Excel annexes is intended to facilitate data analysis and transparency about ongoing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance documents: CHMP rules of procedure and work plan
rubrics_metrics.description: For full details, see the CHMP rules of procedure and work plan (e.g. 'CHMP rules of procedure' adopted EMEA/45110/2007 – Revised 09 February 2024; 'CHMP work plan 2026' EMA/CHMP/348308/2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rules of procedure and work plan provide the formal governance, procedural rules and planned activities of CHMP; consult these documents for binding procedural requirements and annual priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee composition and membership
rubrics_metrics.description: CHMP consists of scientific experts appointed by EU Member States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership is based on national appointments of scientific experts; a members list is published and available to view, informing stakeholders about expertise represented on the committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting frequency and scheduling / archival practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee meets once a month. EMA publishes CHMP meeting dates (multi-year lists) and maintains archives of meeting documents (e.g. CHMP meeting archives covering various year ranges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular monthly meetings and published schedules help stakeholders plan submissions and follow CHMP work; archives provide historical records of decisions and meeting outputs.
